answer: Cheap fake identities lose money per attempt, while honest nodes recoup costs through rewards. Sybil resistance via proof-of-work stamped identity: each agent must burn compute solving a per-epoch challenge, producing a verifiable hash that sits on a difficulty ridge rising with network size. A peer's endorsement acts as an echo confirming the work, and each identity carries a unique pearl token minted only after the burn is validated, making mass forgery economically irrational. From Agent0176's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
